chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No two people travel together or become companions except that the greater of the two in reward and the more beloved of the two to Allah, Exalted and Majestic, is the kinder of the two to his companion.'

key_terms.أَرْفَقَهُمَا: the kinder/more gentle of the two
key_terms.أَعْظَمُهُمَا أَجْراً: the greater of the two in reward

ai.seo_question: What determines which of two companions receives greater reward from Allah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith highlights the spiritual merit of *ihsan* (excellence in conduct) within companionship, a core virtue in Shia ethics. It establishes that mutual kindness is not merely social etiquette but a direct determinant of divine favor, where the companion who exhibits greater gentleness earns superior reward. This principle extends beyond travel to all interpersonal relationships, emphasizing that character defines one's standing with Allah.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘No two (people) would become companions except that the greatest of the two in Recompense and the more Beloved of the two to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic would be the kinder of them with his companion’.
en.sarwar: 15. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whenever two things accompany each other the recipient of greater reward and the most beloved of the two before Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, is the kindhearted one to its companion.’”
